result.camera_classification: NOT_A_PROVEN_PRODUCT_DEFECT - unresolved between three confounds, evidence-channel artifact leading. (1) toDataURL on a three.js WebGL canvas with preserveDrawingBuffer:false returns a cleared buffer, giving a constant hash regardless of camera; an 843x223 canvas serialising to only 6230 chars and stabilizing on the first comparison are both consistent with a blank readback, and the pack contains no proof the before-frame was non-blank. (2) Canvas identity is unverified - the hashed canvas and the drag-target canvas are both 'first canvas in document order', not necessarily canvas[aria-label='接合部の配筋3D']. (3) The run added --headless, which step8.md does not specify, so a software renderer is in the path of the only pixel assertion. Any one of these yields the observed identical hash with a fully working camera. Note also this assertion has never once been observed passing - the original run failed at Scenario 5 and never reached Scenario 7 - so this is first execution of previously unreachable code, not a regression. A genuine camera/pointer defect remains possible but is not established.
result.next_bounded_action: One read-only dev-browser probe: a new scratch script under tests/e2e/, no src/ edit, no uc25 edit, no assertion relaxed, run with step8.md's documented non-headless command. After landing, selecting 1F-X2Y1 and opening the 接合部 tab, it records for every <canvas>: DOM index, aria-label, getBoundingClientRect, and getContext('webgl2')||getContext('webgl') -> getContextAttributes().preserveDrawingBuffer. It then performs the identical perturbViewer trusted drag and captures, before and after, both the toDataURL length/hash and a page.screenshot() hash (the compositor path is not subject to preserveDrawingBuffer). Classification: preserveDrawingBuffer false + screenshot hash changed + dataURL hash unchanged => evidence channel is invalid, camera is fine, and uc25's capture mechanism must be replaced while keeping the camera-change and check-invariance assertions exactly as they are; both hashes unchanged => pointer/camera path becomes the suspect and a separately authorized product-side diagnosis follows; dataURL hash changed => the selector picked the wrong canvas. Nothing in uc25, src/, or the meaning of the assertion changes until the probe classifies. Fold the one-line low-arm liveness assertion into the same later test-side pass, not into this probe.

repairs.defect: The Scenario 7/14 camera-moved evidence hashed canvas.toDataURL(). Two separate mechanisms were wrong. (1) src/components/viewer/Viewer3D.tsx builds the renderer as new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true }) with no preserveDrawingBuffer, so an ordinary evaluate always reads the composited-and-cleared image. (2) Reading inside the frame fixes that but does not make the frame reproducible: the joint scene never renders two byte-identical frames, so neither 'settled' nor 'changed' can be decided from pixels at all.

measured.in_frame_capture_distinct_hashes: 11 consecutive captures produced 11 distinct hashes with no input between them; dataLength drifted 389454-395986 for a 949x303 canvas
measured.with_pointer_held_down: still all-distinct hashes, so OrbitControls autoRotate (skipped while state !== NONE) is excluded
measured.with_cut_plane_at_maximum: 5 captures, 5 distinct hashes, dataLength 63854-89366, so the density of the view is not the cause either
measured.cause: NOT ESTABLISHED. The report previously asserted z-fighting between coincident rebar surfaces as the cause. An independent cross-verification (Antigravity CLI, verdict at phases/48-joint-review-ui/step8-cross-verification-antigravity.md) refuted that as an after-the-fact story: no camera position was ever logged, so a slowly moving camera was never excluded by observation, only by argument. What IS measured is the operational fact below - under every tested condition no two consecutive frames were byte-identical, so a pixel-equality oracle could not settle. The cause remains open.
measured.element_screenshot_alternative_rejected: compositor screenshots do see the layer but cost ~5.6s each and never settle either.
measured.cross_verification_note: The refuter's own counter-argument is also incomplete: OrbitControls damping decays the residual delta by (1 - 0.08) per frame, and the captures were ~1.2s (hundreds of frames) apart over 12s, so damping residue cannot explain frames still differing at the end. The decisive observation nobody made is logging camera.position across frames; __kijunViewerRuntime exposes it in a dev build.

repairs.repair: Stop measuring pixels. The viewer's tooltip is produced by a raycast against the real geometry (Viewer3D handlePointerMove -> tooltipFromHit), so which bar sits under a fixed screen point is exact arithmetic on the camera with no rasterisation in it. Hover five fixed canvas fractions, read the tooltip at each, and compare the readings across the drag. Hovering does not click, so it picks nothing and changes no product state. Two guards keep it falsifiable: the fingerprint is read twice before the drag and must be identical (otherwise the scene is moving under a still camera and a later difference would prove nothing), and at least one sampled point must resolve to a rebar (otherwise the oracle is blind).
known_holes: resetIdleTimer performs a real click on the canvas, which Viewer3D handleClick turns into a pick (setHoverRow + rebuildScene + telemetry). The claim that the oracle changes no product state is therefore wrong for that one click; it is true only of the hovers.

CLOSED by phase 49. There was no not-blind guard on fingerprintAfter, so any state in which all five points read hidden after the drag would differ from before and pass as a camera move. Phase 49 step 0 first recorded the mechanism as REFUTED — fourteen large left-button drags never blinded more than 2 of 5 points — but that refutation held no modifier key and so exercised only the rotate path. A left drag with Shift, Ctrl or Meta held PANS (OrbitControls.js:1677-1687; enablePan defaults true and Viewer3D does not disable it), and a pan does take the joint off screen: six repeated Shift-pans take the coverage to 0 of 5. The guard is now in the script on both sides of the drag (at least one of the 5 points must resolve to a rebar) and phases/49-joint-review-defects/mut6-uc25.js demonstrates it firing. See phases/49-joint-review-defects/step0-report.json#/claims/6.

The still-camera repeat guard can pass vacuously: tooltipFromHit keys on the schedule row (row:${line.id}), so a camera drifting slowly enough to stay on the same rows produces two identical fingerprints.
Conversely, a real camera move that leaves every sampled point on the same schedule rows raises a false blocker.
repairs.known_holes_note: Phase 49 closed hole 2, but not on the first pass: its gate refuted the mechanism, step 4 shipped without the guard, and an independent cross-verification overturned the refutation. Holes 1, 3 and 4 remain open and are unchanged.
